title: Qualitative primary data research on care needs and oncological diseases: Theoretical and methodological advances in nursing research in Germany
summary:
The PoWEr-QualiPrim sub-project aims to describe the progression of care for adult patients diagnosed with cancer. To this end, individual symptoms, co-existing chronic conditions, available resources and stress factors are systematically recorded. The data is collected using two methods: narrative interviews are conducted in which participants describe their illness and care situation chronologically. Diary logs are kept over a period of fourteen days, documenting daily experiences, support needs and subjective well-being.

The data obtained is analysed using grounded theory methodology. In this process, the texts are first broken down into individual units of meaning, then summarised into thematic categories, and finally key categories are identified, which form the basis for a care theory regarding the care trajectories of people with cancer who require care. These qualitative categories are then linked to the quantitative data from the overall project to obtain a comprehensive picture of care pathways. At the same time, the study examines the extent to which the diary method is practicable and beneficial in research-intensive, externally funded projects involving vulnerable target groups.
conditions: People with cancer (all types) who require care

interventions.name: People with cancer who require care daily describe their care experiences over the course of 14 days using a diary-method
People with cancer who require care describe their care experiences retrospectively in narrative interviews

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Confirmed oncological diagnosis
- Sufficient german language skills 
- Existing self-care deficit (care level or self-reported dependence on others in daily life)
Exclusion criteria:
None
